name: CORS misconfiguration allowing credentialed cross-origin reads
requires: an endpoint that returns sensitive, session-scoped data as JSON
the ability to send an arbitrary Origin header and read the response headers
for an impact claim: a session carried in a cookie the browser attaches automatically
questions: Does the response reflect an arbitrary attacker-supplied Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, or return a fixed value, or omit the header entirely?
Is Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true on that same response, which is what turns reflection into a cross-origin credentialed read?
Is the reflected origin matched against an allowlist by exact string comparison, or by a prefix, suffix, or regex a lookalike domain can satisfy?
Does the endpoint also answer a preflight with the requested method and headers allowed, or does the credentialed read fail at OPTIONS?
Is Origin: null accepted with credentials, which a sandboxed iframe or a data URL can supply without any attacker domain?
Does the response carry Vary: Origin, or will a shared cache serve one origin's ACAO header to a different origin?
Is the session credential a cookie with SameSite=None, so the browser will attach it on a cross-site fetch from the attacker page?
Does the data returned differ per user, or is it identical for every caller and therefore already public?
false_positives: ACAO reflects the origin but Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is absent or false, so the browser blocks credentialed reads
The endpoint requires an Authorization header, which an attacker page cannot set cross-origin without its own token
The allowlist compares the parsed origin host exactly, and every lookalike attempt fails the comparison
The data returned is identical for anonymous and authenticated callers, so a cross-origin read reveals nothing
The wildcard ACAO is returned with credentials false, which is the standards-compliant public-API configuration
The preflight rejects the attacker origin's method or headers, so the actual request is never sent
poc_must_show: the full response headers for a request carrying our controlled Origin, with ACAO and ACAC both quoted
the same endpoint with a benign Origin, showing the header either absent or restricted to the legitimate origin
for impact, a browser page on our origin that reads the response body cross-origin and displays authenticated data
the cookie attributes of the session being read, showing the browser would attach it cross-site
confirmation the endpoint is not returning identical public data to an unauthenticated caller
impact_bar: a browser on an attacker-controlled origin reads authenticated, user-specific response content, demonstrated with reflected-origin plus credentials plus a real cross-origin read
